title.zh: 卷38 列傳第30 蘇亮 柳虯 呂思禮 薛憕 薛寘 李昶 元偉
title.en: Volume 38 Biographies 30: Su Liang; Liu Qiu; Lu Sili; Xue Cheng; Xue Zhi; Li Chang; Yuan Wei
title.raw: 卷38 列傳第30 蘇亮 柳虯 呂思禮 薛憕 薛寘 李昶 元偉 Volume 38 Biographies 30: Su Liang; Liu Qiu; Lu Sili; Xue Cheng; Xue Zhi; Li Chang; Yuan Wei

sentences.zh: 蘇亮 弟湛 柳虯 呂思禮 薛憕 薛寘 李昶 元偉

translations.literal: Su Liang; younger brother Zhan; Liu Qiu; Lu Sili; Xue Cheng; Xue Zhi; Li Chang; Yuan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Liang; his younger brother Zhan; Liu Qiu; Lu Sili; Xue Cheng; Xue Zhi; Li Chang; and Yuan Wei.

sentences.zh: 蘇亮字景順，武功人也。

translations.literal: Su Liang, styled Jingshun, was a man of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Su Liang, courtesy name Jingshun, came from Wugong.

sentences.zh: 祖權，魏中書侍郎、玉門郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Wei Secretariat Gentleman and Administrator of Yumen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan had served Wei as secretariat gentleman and administrator of Yumen commandery.

sentences.zh: 父佑，泰山郡守。

translations.literal: His father You was Administrator of Taishan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was administrator of Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 亮少通敏，博學，好屬文，善章奏。

translations.literal: Liang in youth was penetrating and quick; broadly learned; fond of literary composition; skilled at memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Liang was quick-witted and perceptive, widely read, fond of writing, and adept at formal memorials.

sentences.zh: 初舉秀才，至洛陽，遇河內常景。

translations.literal: At first recommended as xiucai, he reached Luoyang and met Chang Jing of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When first nominated as a xiucai candidate, he went to Luoyang and there met Chang Jing of Henei.

sentences.zh: 景深器之，退而謂人曰：「秦中才學可以抗山東者，將此人乎。

translations.literal: Jing deeply prized him; withdrawing he told others: "Among the talents and learning of the Qin region who can match those of the Shandong region — is it perhaps this man?
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing thought highly of him; afterward he said to others, "Among the learned men of the Qin lands who can stand against those of the east — could it be this one?

sentences.zh: 」魏齊王蕭寶夤引為參軍。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Qi of Wei, Xiao Baoyin, recruited him as military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi under Wei, brought him on as a military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 後寶夤開府，復為其府主薄。

translations.literal: Later when Baoyin opened a headquarters, he again became its headquarters registrar.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin later established a headquarters, Liang again served as its chief registrar.

sentences.zh: 從寶夤西征，轉記室參軍。

translations.literal: Following Baoyin on the western campaign, he was transferred to recording-secretary adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Baoyin on the western expedition and was moved to recording secretary on the staff.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遷大將軍，仍為之掾。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was promoted grand general, he still served as his staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rose to grand general, Liang remained on his staff.

sentences.zh: 寶夤雅知重亮，凡有文檄謀議，皆以委之。

translations.literal: Baoyin had long known and valued Liang; whatever documents, proclamations, or strategic deliberations there were, he entrusted them all to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin had long esteemed Liang; every dispatch, proclamation, and plan passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 尋行武功郡事，甚著聲績。

translations.literal: Before long he acted in Wugong commandery affairs and greatly showed reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was administering Wugong commandery and won a strong reputation for his work.

sentences.zh: 寶夤作亂，以亮為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, he made Liang Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rose in rebellion, he appointed Liang gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 亮善處人間，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Liang was skilled in dealing among people and had no friction with things.
translations.idiomatic: Liang handled people well and gave offense to no one.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤敗，從之者遇禍，唯亮獲全。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, those who followed him met disaster; only Liang was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin fell, his followers were ruined; Liang alone escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 乃長孫稚、爾朱天光等西討，竝以亮為郎中，專典文翰。

translations.literal: Then Changsun Zhi, Erzhu Tianguang, and others campaigned west; all made Liang gentleman of the palace, specially in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsun Zhi, Erzhu Tianguang, and others marched west, each made Liang a palace gentleman in sole charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮軍將軍、光祿大夫、散騎常侍、岐州大中正。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to general who stabilizes the army, grand master for splendid happiness, attendant cavalier at leisure, and chief rectifier of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to general who stabilizes the army, grand master for splendid happiness, attendant cavalier at leisure, and chief rectifier of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳為關西行臺，引亮為左丞，典機密。

translations.literal: Heba Yue became western mobile headquarters in Guanzhong and recruited Liang as left aide, in charge of confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue took the western mobile headquarters in Guanzhong, he made Liang his left aide and entrusted him with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，除吏部郎中，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was appointed gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, with added ranks of general of the guard and right grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fled west, Liang was made a gentleman of the ministry of personnel, with added ranks of general of the guard and right grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，拜給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was appointed Attending Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and concurrently led as Secretariat Aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he became attending gentleman at the yellow gate and also served as secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝子宜都王式為秦州刺史，以亮為司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei's son Prince Yidu Shi became Inspector of Qin Province; Liang was made his chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei's son, Prince Yidu Shi, became inspector of Qin Province, Liang was appointed his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 帝謂亮曰：「黃門侍郎豈可為秦州司馬，直以朕愛子出蕃，故以心腹相委，勿以為恨。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Liang: "Could a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate simply be Chief Administrator of Qin Province? It is only because my beloved son goes out to his fief that I entrust him to a trusted confidant — do not take it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Liang, "A gentleman at the yellow gate is hardly meant to be chief administrator of Qin Province. I send my beloved son to his fief and therefore place him in the hands of a trusted man — do not take it as a slight.

sentences.zh: 」臨辭，賜以御馬。

translations.literal: " At parting from farewell, he was granted an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: " At their parting the emperor gave him an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 七年，復為黃門郎，加驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he again became Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, with added rank of General of Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to gentleman at the yellow gate with the added rank of general of rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷都官尚書、使持節、行北華州刺史，封臨涇縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Minister Director in the Ministry of Justice, granted credentials, and acted as Inspector of Northern Hua Province; enfeoffed as Viscount of Linjing county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became minister director in the ministry of justice, received credentials, and acted as inspector of Northern Hua Province; he was enfeoffed as viscount of Linjing county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除中書監，領著作，修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat, concurrently leading the works directorate, editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the secretariat, concurrently supervising the works directorate and editing the national history.

sentences.zh: 亮有機辯，善談笑。

translations.literal: Liang had quick wit and eloquence; he was skilled in jest and conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was quick-witted and fluent, and delighted in easy talk and laughter.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚重之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 有所籌議，率多會旨。

translations.literal: In whatever deliberations there were, he generally accorded with the intent.
translations.idiomatic: In council he usually grasped the point at once.

sentences.zh: 記人之善，忘人之過。

translations.literal: He remembered people's good points and forgot people's faults.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered others' virtues and overlooked their failings.

sentences.zh: 薦達後進，常如弗及。

translations.literal: He recommended and advanced junior men, always as if he himself could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted younger men ahead of him as though he himself could never catch up.

sentences.zh: 故當世敬慕焉。

translations.literal: For this reason the age revered and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: For this his contemporaries honored and admired him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除秘書監、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，尋拜大行臺尚書，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat archives, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes; soon after appointed Minister of the Grand Mobile Headquarters and sent out as Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became director of the secretariat archives, general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in protocol to the three dukes; soon after he was made minister of the grand mobile headquarters and sent out as inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其作牧本州，特給路車、鼓吹，先還其宅，幷給騎士三千。

translations.literal: The court, because he was governing his home province, specially granted a ceremonial chariot and musicians, first restored his residence, and also provided three thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was returning to govern his home province, the court gave him a state carriage and musicians, had his house prepared in advance, and supplied three thousand mounted escorts.

sentences.zh: 列羽儀，遊鄉黨，經過故人，歡飲旬日，然後入州。

translations.literal: He arrayed feathered insignia, toured his home district, passed by old friends, drank and rejoiced for ten days, then entered the province.
translations.idiomatic: With full ceremonial display he traveled through his native district, stopping to feast with old friends for ten days before entering the province.

sentences.zh: 世以為榮。

translations.literal: The age regarded this as glory.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time took this as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 十七年，征拜侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was summoned and appointed Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was recalled and made palace companion.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post.

sentences.zh: 贈本官。

translations.literal: Posthumously given his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his last title.

sentences.zh: 亮少與從弟綽俱知名。

translations.literal: Liang in youth together with his younger cousin Chuo were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Liang and his younger cousin Chuo were both well known.

sentences.zh: 然綽文章少不逮亮，至於經畫進趣，亮又減之。

translations.literal: Yet Chuo's literary compositions were somewhat inferior to Liang's; as for planning and advancement, Liang again fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's writing was a little less accomplished than Liang's, but in strategy and advancement Liang fell short of him.

sentences.zh: 故世稱二蘇焉。

translations.literal: Hence the age called them the Two Sus.
translations.idiomatic: People therefore spoke of them as the Two Sus.

sentences.zh: 亮自大統以來，無歲不轉官，一年或至三遷。

translations.literal: From Datong onward Liang had not a year without transfer of office; in one year he might reach as many as three promotions.
translations.idiomatic: From the Datong era onward Liang was promoted every year, sometimes three times in a single year.

sentences.zh: 僉曰才至，不怪其速也。

translations.literal: All said talent had arrived and did not wonder at the speed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed his talent had come into its own and did not marvel at the pace.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆數十篇，頗行於世。

translations.literal: The compositions he wrote numbered several tens of pieces and circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left several dozen literary pieces that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子師嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi inherited his place.

sentences.zh: 以亮名重於時，起家為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Because Liang's name was weighty in the age, Shi began his career as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang's reputation stood high in his day, Shi entered office directly as gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 亮弟湛，字景儁。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Zhan, styled Jingjun.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Zhan, courtesy name Jingjun.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，與亮俱著名西土。

translations.literal: In youth he had will and conduct; together with Liang he was renowned in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed purpose and integrity, and together with Liang he was famous throughout the west.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，舉秀才，除奉朝請，領侍御史，加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At over twenty years of age he was recommended as xiucai, appointed attendant at court audiences, concurrently serving as palace censor, with added rank of supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he was nominated as xiucai, made attendant at court audiences and palace censor, and given the added rank of supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤西討，以湛為行臺郎中，深見委任。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, he made Zhan Mobile Headquarters Gentleman and deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiao Baoyin's western campaign, Zhan was made mobile headquarters gentleman and deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤將謀叛逆，湛時臥疾於家。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was about to plot rebellion, Zhan at the time lay ill at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was preparing to rebel, Zhan was confined to his home by illness.

sentences.zh: 寶夤乃令湛從母弟天水姜儉謂湛曰：「吾不能坐受死亡，今便為身計，不復作魏臣也。

translations.literal: Baoyin then had Zhan's maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui tell Zhan: "I cannot sit and receive death; now I will plan for my own body and will no longer be a minister of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sent Zhan's maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui to tell him, "I cannot sit here and wait to die. I must now look to my own survival and will no longer serve Wei.

sentences.zh: 與卿死生榮辱，方當共之，故以相報。

translations.literal: Life and death, honor and shame — I am about to share them with you, and therefore inform you.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever life or death, honor or disgrace may bring, we shall share it together — that is why I tell you now.

sentences.zh: 」湛聞之，舉聲大哭。

translations.literal: " When Zhan heard this, he raised his voice and wept loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhan heard this he burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 儉遽止之曰：「何得便爾？

translations.literal: Jian hastily stopped him and said: "How can you at once be thus?
translations.idiomatic: Jian quickly hushed him and said, "How can you react like that at once?

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「闔門百口，卽時屠滅，云何不哭。

translations.literal: " Zhan said: "A whole household of a hundred mouths — instantly to be slaughtered and wiped out — how could I not weep?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan said, "A household of a hundred souls faces immediate slaughter — how could I not weep?

sentences.zh: 」哭數十聲，徐謂儉曰：「為我白齊王，王本以窮而歸人，賴朝廷假王羽翼，遂得榮寵至此。

translations.literal: " After weeping dozens of cries, he slowly told Jian: "Speak to the Prince of Qi for me: the Prince originally came to others in poverty; relying on the court lending him wings, he reached such glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: " After weeping many times he said slowly to Jian, "Tell the Prince of Qi for me: he came to the court in poverty, and only by the throne's support did he rise to such honor.

sentences.zh: 旣屬國步多虞，不能竭誠報德，豈可乘人間隙，便有問鼎之心乎。

translations.literal: Now that the nation's step has many anxieties, unable to exhaust sincerity in repaying grace — how could one seize an opening in affairs and suddenly harbor the heart to wrest the tripod?
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is full of troubles, and instead of repaying grace with full loyalty, would he seize a moment of weakness and aspire to seize the throne?

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改。

translations.literal: Now Wei's virtue though declining, Heaven's mandate has not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's power may be waning, but Heaven's mandate has not yet shifted.

sentences.zh: 王之恩義，未洽於民，破亡之期，必不旋踵。

translations.literal: The Prince's grace and righteousness have not permeated the people; the term of defeat and ruin will surely arrive in no time.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's kindness has not won the people's hearts, and ruin will come upon him almost at once.

sentences.zh: 蘇湛終不能以積世忠貞之基，一旦為王族滅也。

translations.literal: Su Zhan ultimately cannot, on a foundation of accumulated generations of loyalty and steadfastness, in one morning have his clan destroyed for the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhan cannot throw away generations of loyal service and see his whole clan destroyed for the prince's sake.

sentences.zh: 」寶夤復令儉謂湛曰：「此是救命之計，不得不爾。

translations.literal: " Baoyin again had Jian tell Zhan: "This is a plan to save life — it cannot be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyin again sent Jian to say, "This is a plan to save our lives — there is no other way.

sentences.zh: 」湛復曰：「凡舉大事，當得天下奇士。

translations.literal: " Zhan replied again: "Whenever one undertakes a great affair, one ought to obtain the world's extraordinary talents.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan answered again, "Any great undertaking needs the rarest men in the realm.

sentences.zh: 今但共長安博徒小兒輩為此計，豈有辦哉。

translations.literal: Now one only joins with Chang'an gambling-house lads and petty youths in this plan — could it succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you would carry this out with Chang'an gamblers and street boys — how could it succeed?

sentences.zh: 湛不忍見荊棘生王戶庭也。

translations.literal: Zhan cannot bear to see brambles grow in the Prince's household courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan cannot bear to see thorns spring up in the prince's own courtyard.

sentences.zh: 願賜骸骨還舊裏，庶歸全地下，無愧先人。

translations.literal: I wish to be granted my bones to return to my old home, that I may return whole beneath the ground and be without shame before my forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me leave to go home and die in peace, that I may lie whole beneath the earth without shaming my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」寶夤素重之，知必不為己用，遂聽還武功。

translations.literal: " Baoyin had long valued him and knew he would never serve him; he thereupon allowed him to return to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyin had always respected him and knew he would never be won over, so he let him return to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後果敗。

translations.literal: Baoyin afterward indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was defeated soon after.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝卽位，徵拜尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zhan was summoned and appointed Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Zhan was summoned and made a gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂之曰：「聞卿答蕭寶夤，甚有美辭，可為我說之也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to him: "I hear your reply to Xiao Baoyin had very fine wording — you may tell it to me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to him, "I hear your answer to Xiao Baoyin was eloquent — tell me what you said.

sentences.zh: 」湛頓首謝曰：「臣自惟言辭不如伍被遠矣，然始終不易，竊謂過之。

translations.literal: " Zhan bowed and said: "Your subject considers that in wording I am far inferior to Wu Bei; yet in unchanging from beginning to end, I privately think I surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan bowed and said, "I am far less eloquent than Wu Bei, but in holding firm from first to last I believe I surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 但臣與寶夤周旋契闊，言得盡心，而不能令其守節，此臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Only that your subject mingled long with Baoyin in intimate association and spoke with full heart, yet could not make him hold to integrity — that is your subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I moved among Baoyin's circle for years and spoke my mind fully, and still could not keep him loyal — that is my fault.

sentences.zh: 」孝莊大悅，加授散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: " Xiaozhuang was greatly pleased and additionally appointed him attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaozhuang was greatly pleased and additionally made him attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，以疾還鄉里，終於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, on account of illness he returned to his home district and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he went home on account of illness and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously given attendant cavalier at leisure, general who pacifies the west, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted attendant cavalier at leisure, general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 湛弟讓，字景恕。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Rang, styled Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Rang, courtesy name Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，好學，頗有人倫鑒識。

translations.literal: In youth clever and perceptive, fond of learning, with considerable discernment in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bright and eager to learn, with a keen eye for character.

sentences.zh: 初為本州主薄，稍遷別駕、武都郡守、鎮遠將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At first he was registrar of his home province; gradually promoted to vice-director, Administrator of Wudu commandery, general who pacifies the distance, and grand master with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registrar of his home province and rose step by step to vice-director, administrator of Wudu commandery, general who pacifies the distance, and grand master with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及太祖為丞相，引為府屬，甚見親待。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became chancellor, he recruited Rang as headquarters staff and treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became chancellor, he brought Rang onto his staff and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 出為衛將軍、南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as general of the guard and Inspector of Southern Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as general of the guard and inspector of Southern Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 治有善政。

translations.literal: His governance had good policies.
translations.idiomatic: His administration won praise for sound policy.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office not long after.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted general of chariots and cavalry, equal in protocol to the three dukes, and inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 柳虯字仲蟠，司會慶之兄也。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, styled Zhongpan, was elder brother of Liu Qing, Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, courtesy name Zhongpan, was elder brother of Liu Qing, director of revenue.

sentences.zh: 年十三，便專精好學。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he already devoted himself wholly to love of learning.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was already wholly absorbed in study.

sentences.zh: 時貴游子弟就學者，竝車服華盛，唯虯不事容飾。

translations.literal: At the time the sons of noble clans who came to study all had splendid carriages and dress; only Qiu did not indulge in adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of great families who came to study all arrived in splendid carriages and dress; Qiu alone wore no finery.

sentences.zh: 遍

translations.literal: Thoroughly
translations.idiomatic: He studied

translations.literal: (授) [emended: 受]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: received]

sentences.zh: 〔受〕《五經》，略通大義，兼博涉子史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: 〔受〕 The Five Classics — he grasped their broad meaning in outline; he also broadly read the masters and histories; he was fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: the Five Classics and grasped their broad meaning; he also read widely in the masters and histories and loved to write.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，揚州刺史李憲舉虯秀才，兗州刺史馮儁引虯為府主薄。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, Li Xian, Inspector of Yang Province, recommended Qiu as xiucai; Feng Jun, Inspector of Yan Province, recruited Qiu as headquarters registrar.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era Li Xian, inspector of Yang Province, nominated Qiu as xiucai, and Feng Jun, inspector of Yan Province, made him headquarters registrar.

sentences.zh: 旣而樊子鵠為吏部尚書，其兄義為揚州。

translations.literal: Before long Fan Zihu became Minister of Personnel; his elder brother Yi was Inspector of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fan Zihu became minister of personnel, and his elder brother Yi became inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 治中，加鎮遠將軍，非其好也，遂棄官還洛陽。

translations.literal: Province director of governance, with added rank general who pacifies the distance — not to his liking; he thereupon abandoned office and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was made provincial director of governance with the added rank of general who pacifies the distance, but the post did not suit him, so he resigned and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 屬天下喪亂，乃退耕於陽城，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Amid universal disorder of the realm, he withdrew to farm at Yangcheng, with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire fell into chaos, he retired to farm at Yangcheng and meant to live out his days there.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，馮翊王元季海、領軍獨孤信鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai and army commander Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai and army commander Dugu Xin held Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 于時舊京荒廢，人物罕極，唯有虯在陽城，裴諏在潁川。

translations.literal: At that time the old capital was desolate and ruined; men and affairs were extremely scarce; only Qiu was at Yangcheng and Pei Sou at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The old capital was then waste and empty, with scarcely a soul left; only Qiu remained at Yangcheng and Pei Sou at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 信等乃俱徵之，以虯為行臺郎中，諏為都督府屬，並掌文翰。

translations.literal: Xin and the others then summoned both; they made Qiu Mobile Headquarters Gentleman and Sou aide in the command headquarters, both in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and his colleagues summoned them both, making Qiu mobile headquarters gentleman and Sou an aide in the command headquarters, each in charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「北府裴諏，南省柳虯。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying about them: "Pei Sou of the Northern Headquarters, Liu Qiu of the Southern Secretariat. Since autonomy
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said of them, "Pei Sou of the northern headquarters, Liu Qiu of the southern secretariat. Since they took charge

sentences.zh: 」時軍旅務殷，虯勵精從事，或通夜不寢。

translations.literal: military affairs were pressing; Qiu applied himself with tireless zeal and sometimes went the whole night without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: military affairs were fully engaged; Qiu drove himself with tireless zeal and sometimes worked through the night without sleep.

sentences.zh: 季海嘗云：「柳郎中判事，我不復重看。

translations.literal: Jihai once said: "When Director Qiu of the Bureau judges a case, I need never look again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jihai once remarked, "When Director Qiu of the Bureau decides a case, I never need to review it.

sentences.zh: 」四年，入朝，太祖欲官之，虯辭母老，乞侍醫藥。

translations.literal: " In year 4 he entered court; the Grand Progenitor wished to give him office, but Qiu pleaded that his mother was old and begged leave to attend her with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: " In Datong year 4 he came to court. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to appoint him, but Qiu pleaded that his mother was aged and asked leave to care for her and see to her medicine.

sentences.zh: 太祖許焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai consented.

sentences.zh: 久之為獨孤信開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: After some time he became opening-office attendant of Dugu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became opening-office attendant on Dugu Xin's staff.

sentences.zh: 信出鎮隴右，因為秦州刺史，以虯為二府司馬。

translations.literal: When Xin went out to garrison Longyou, he was also made Inspector of Qin Province, and Qiu was made marshal of the two offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin went west to garrison Longyou and was made inspector of Qin Province, Liu Qiu was appointed marshal of both offices.

sentences.zh: 雖處元僚，不綜府事，唯在信左右談論而已。

translations.literal: Though he held the chief staff rank, he did not oversee the office's affairs; he only discussed and debated at Xin's side.
translations.idiomatic: Although he held a chief staff post, he did not manage the office's business and only talked and debated at Dugu Xin's side.

sentences.zh: 因使見太祖，被留為丞相府記室。

translations.literal: On an embassy he was received in audience by the Grand Progenitor and was kept as recording officer in the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on embassy to see Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, he was detained and made recording officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 追論歸朝功，封美陽縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: His merit in returning to court was reviewed; he was enfeoffed Baron of Meiyang county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His service in returning to court was rewarded with enfeoffment as baron of Meiyang, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 虯以史官密書善惡，未足懲勸。

translations.literal: Qiu considered that when historiographers secretly recorded good and ill, it was not enough to warn and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu felt that when historiographers kept good and ill secret in their records, the practice fell short of warning and encouraging men.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古者人君立史官，非但記事而已，蓋所以為監誡也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when rulers established historiographers, it was not merely to record events; it was meant to serve as oversight and warning.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity rulers appointed historiographers not merely to keep records, but to serve as monitors and warnings.

sentences.zh: 動則左史書之，言則右史書之，彰善癉惡，以樹風聲。

translations.literal: When they acted, the left historiographer wrote it; when they spoke, the right historiographer wrote it — making good bright and evil foul, to set the tone for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds were written by the left historiographer and their words by the right, making virtue shine and vice stink, so as to set the moral tone of the age.

sentences.zh: 故南史抗節，表崔杼之罪；

translations.literal: Hence the attendant of Southern History resisted to the end and laid bare Cui Zhu's crime;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the attendant of Southern History held firm and exposed Cui Zhu's crime;

sentences.zh: 董狐書法，明趙盾之愆。

translations.literal: Dong Hu's brush in the records made Zhao Dun's fault clear.
translations.idiomatic: and Dong Hu's brush in the records made Zhao Dun's fault plain.

sentences.zh: 是知直筆於朝，其來久矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows that straightforward writing at court has a long history.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that honest writing at court is no new thing.

sentences.zh: 而漢魏已還，密為記注，徒聞後世，無益當時，非所謂將順其美，匡救其惡者也。

translations.literal: Yet from Han and Wei onward records were kept in secret; later ages alone heard of them, with no benefit to the present — this is not what is meant by supporting what is beautiful and correcting what is evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Han and Wei onward annals were kept in secret, heard only by later ages and of no use to the living — not the meaning of supporting what is good and correcting what is wrong.

sentences.zh: 且著述之人，密書其事，縱能直筆，人莫之知。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who compose records secretly write events; even if the brush is straight, no one knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who write history do so in secret; even when the brush is honest, no one knows it.

sentences.zh: 何止物生橫議，亦自異端互起。

translations.literal: How much more do wild opinions arise among men, and heresies contend with one another!
translations.idiomatic: Wild talk spreads among men, and rival doctrines spring up on every side.

sentences.zh: 故班固致受金之名，陳壽有求米之論。

translations.literal: Hence Ban Gu earned the name of taking gold, and Chen Shou the talk of begging for rice.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Ban Gu was accused of taking bribes, and Chen Shou of begging for grain.

sentences.zh: 著漢魏者，非一氏；

translations.literal: Those who wrote on Han and Wei were not of one house;
translations.idiomatic: Those who wrote histories of Han and Wei were not of one house;

sentences.zh: 造晉史者，至數家。

translations.literal: those who compiled Jin history reached several families.
translations.idiomatic: and compilers of Jin history numbered several families.

sentences.zh: 後代紛紜，莫知准的。

translations.literal: Later generations were confused and knew no standard.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages were tangled in dispute and knew no standard.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下則天稽古，勞心庶政。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, in accord with Heaven, examines antiquity and toils over the myriad affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, in accord with Heaven, examines antiquity and labors over the myriad affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 開誹謗之路，納忠讜之言。

translations.literal: You have opened the road of criticism and received loyal and forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: You have opened the way to criticism and receive loyal and forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 諸史官記事者，請皆當朝顯言其狀，然後付之史閣。

translations.literal: I ask that all historiographers who record events speak their accounts openly at court, and only then entrust them to the historiographical archive.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all historiographers who record events state their accounts openly at court, and only then deposit them in the historiographical archive.

sentences.zh: 庶令是非明著，得失無隱。

translations.literal: Thus right and wrong may stand clear, and gain and loss be without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Then right and wrong may stand clear, and gain and loss go undisguised.

sentences.zh: 使聞善者日修，有過者知懼。

translations.literal: Let those who hear of good daily improve themselves, and those who have faults know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Let those who hear of virtue daily improve themselves, and those at fault know fear.

sentences.zh: 敢以愚管，輕冒上聞。

translations.literal: I dare, with my narrow view, lightly to intrude this upon Your Majesty's notice.
translations.idiomatic: I dare, with my narrow view, lightly to lay this before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 乞以瞽言，訪之衆議。

translations.literal: I beg that this blind man's words be put before the assembly for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that these blind man's words be submitted to the assembly for discussion.

sentences.zh: 事遂施行。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was thereupon adopted.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除秘書丞。

translations.literal: In year 14 he was appointed secretariat adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 14 he was appointed secretariat adjutant.

sentences.zh: 秘書雖領著作，不參史事，自虯為丞，始令監掌焉。

translations.literal: Though the secretariat oversaw composition, it had not taken part in historiographical affairs; from Qiu's time as adjutant, he was first ordered to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Though the secretariat oversaw composition, it had not handled historiographical affairs; from Liu Qiu's tenure as adjutant, he was first charged to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷中書侍郎，修起居注，仍領丞事。

translations.literal: In year 16 he was transferred to vice director of the secretariat, edited the imperial diary, and still held the adjutant post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was made vice director of the secretariat, edited the imperial diary, and still retained the adjutant post.

sentences.zh: 時人論文體者，有古今之異。

translations.literal: Men of the time who discussed literary style spoke of differences between ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries who debated literary style spoke of differences between ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 虯又以為時有今古，非文有今古，乃為《文質論》。

translations.literal: Qiu also held that times have ancient and modern, but literature does not; he therefore wrote the "Essay on Pattern and Substance."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu also held that times differ between ancient and modern, but literature does not; he therefore wrote the Essay on Pattern and Substance.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: Most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the essay is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，遷秘書監，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Fei of Wei he was transferred to secretariat director, with added ranks General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Fei of Wei's reign he was made secretariat director, with added ranks of general of chariots and cavalry and equal in protocol to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 虯脫略人間，不事小節，弊衣疎食，未嘗改操。

translations.literal: Qiu was free and easy in worldly matters, did not attend to small points, wore worn clothes and ate plain food, and never changed this conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu was indifferent to worldly display, ignored small niceties, wore worn clothes and ate plain food, and never changed that way of life.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之。

translations.literal: Some mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: People jeered at his ways.

sentences.zh: 虯曰：「衣不過適體，食不過充饑。

translations.literal: Qiu said: "Clothes need only fit the body; food need only fill hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu said, "Clothes need only fit the body; food need only fill hunger.

sentences.zh: 孜孜營求，徒勞思慮耳。

translations.literal: To strive and scheme endlessly is only wasted thought.
translations.idiomatic: To strive and scheme without end is only wasted thought.

sentences.zh: 」魏恭帝元年冬，卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: " In the winter of the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: " In the winter of Emperor Gong of Wei's first year he died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰孝。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 有文章數十篇行於世。

translations.literal: Several tens of his essays circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of his essays circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子鴻漸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hongjian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 呂思禮，東平壽張人也。

translations.literal: Lu Sili was a man of Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sili came from Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 性溫潤，不雜交遊。

translations.literal: By nature he was gentle and mild and did not mix in social intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was gentle and mild and kept aloof from casual society.

sentences.zh: 年十四，受學于徐遵明。

translations.literal: At fourteen he received instruction from Xu Zunming.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he studied under Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 長於論難。

translations.literal: He excelled at debate.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for disputation.

sentences.zh: 諸生為之語曰：「講《書》論《易》，其鋒難敵。

translations.literal: The students made a saying of it: "In lecturing on the Documents and debating the Changes, his edge is hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow students had a saying: "In lecturing on the Documents and debating the Changes, his edge is hard to match.

sentences.zh: 」十九，舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: " At nineteen he was nominated as outstanding talent; in the palace examination he ranked at the top.
translations.idiomatic: " At nineteen he was nominated as outstanding talent and ranked at the top in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 除相州功曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed merit officer in the Xiang Province staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed merit officer on the staff of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 葛榮圍鄴，思禮有守禦勳，賜爵平陸縣伯，除欒城令。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong besieged Ye, Sili had merit in defense; he was granted Baron of Pinglu county and appointed magistrate of Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged Ye, Sili won merit in the defense; he was enfeoffed baron of Pinglu and made magistrate of Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，僕射司馬子如薦為尚書二千石郎中。

translations.literal: In the Putai era, Vice Director Sima Ziru recommended him as two-thousand-bushel director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai, Vice Director Sima Ziru recommended him as two-thousand-bushel director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋以地寒被出，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of humble birth, he was dismissed from office and made adjunct erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of humble birth, he was dismissed and made adjunct erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 乃求為關西大。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought appointment under the Guanxi [mobile headquarters — text abbreviated].
translations.idiomatic: He then sought appointment under the Guanxi mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 行臺賀拔岳所重。

translations.literal: The mobile headquarters of Heba Yue valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue's mobile headquarters held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 專掌機密，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: He alone handled confidential affairs and won great repute at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He alone managed secret affairs and won wide acclaim in his day.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，趙貴等議遣赫連達迎太祖，思禮預其謀。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Zhao Gui and others deliberated on sending Helian Da to welcome the Grand Progenitor; Sili took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, Zhao Gui and others resolved to send Helian Da to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; Sili took part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 及太祖為關西大都督，以思禮為府長史，尋除行臺右丞。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became area commander of Guanxi, Sili was made chief clerk of his office; soon he was appointed right assistant director of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became area commander of Guanxi, Sili was made chief clerk of his office; soon he was appointed right assistant director of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以迎魏孝武功，封汝陽縣子，邑四百戶，加冠軍將軍，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: For merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Ruyang county with a fief of four hundred households, promoted to general who exerts majesty, and appointed vice director of the yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward, he was enfeoffed viscount of Ruyang with a fief of four hundred households, promoted to general who exerts majesty, and made vice director of the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝卽位，領著作郎，除安東將軍、都官尚書，兼七兵、殿中二曹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei took the throne, he served as director of composition; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Minister of Justice, and concurrently oversaw the two bureaus of Seven Troops and Palace Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei acceded, he served as director of composition; he was made general who pacifies the east, minister of justice, and concurrently oversaw the bureaus of seven troops and palace hall.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，進爵為侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, he was advanced to marquis with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Tai was captured, he was raised to marquis with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，以謗訕朝政，賜死。

translations.literal: In Datong year 4, for slandering court policy, he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 4, for slandering court policy, he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 思禮好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Sili loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was devoted to learning and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 雖務兼軍國，而手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Though his duties combined military and state affairs, he never put his books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Though military and civil duties both fell to him, he never let go of his books.

sentences.zh: 晝理政事，夜則讀書。

translations.literal: By day he handled government; by night he read.
translations.idiomatic: By day he governed; by night he read.

sentences.zh: 令蒼頭執燭，燭燼夜有數升。

translations.literal: He had a servant hold the candle; the candle drippings each night amounted to several pints.
translations.idiomatic: He had a servant hold the candle; the drippings each night amounted to several pints.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之捷，命為露布，食頃便成。

translations.literal: After the victory at Shaye, he was ordered to draft the victory dispatch, and finished it within the time of a meal.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Shaye, he was ordered to draft the victory dispatch and finished it within the time of a meal.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎其工而且速。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor marveled at his skill and speed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marveled at his skill and speed.

sentences.zh: 所為碑誄表頌，竝傳於世。

translations.literal: The stele inscriptions, dirges, memorials, and eulogies he composed all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The stele inscriptions, dirges, memorials, and eulogies he composed all circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 七年，追贈車騎大將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 7 he was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was posthumously granted general of chariots and cavalry and inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子亶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至駕部下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he reached the post of grand master of the imperial carriage section.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang he had risen to grand master of the imperial carriage section.

sentences.zh: 時有博陵崔騰、新蔡董紹竝早有名譽，歷職清顯。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Teng of Boling and Dong Shao of Xincai alike had early won name and repute and held clear and eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Teng of Boling and Dong Shao of Xincai had both won early renown and held clear, eminent offices.

sentences.zh: 騰為丞相府長史，紹為御史丞。

translations.literal: Teng was chief clerk in the chancellor's office; Shao was assistant director of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was chief clerk in the chancellor's office, and Shao was assistant director of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 俱以投書謗議，賜死。

translations.literal: Both were ordered to die for sending letters of slander and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Both were sentenced to death for sending letters of slander and criticism.

sentences.zh: 薛憕字景猷，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Cheng, styled Jingyou, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cheng, courtesy name Jingyou, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖弘敞，值赫連之亂，率宗人避地襄陽。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hongchang, encountering the turmoil of Helian, led the clan in flight to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hongchang, during the turmoil of Helian, led the clan in flight to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 憕早喪父，家貧，躬耕以養祖母，有暇則覽文籍。

translations.literal: Cheng lost his father early; the family was poor, and he plowed with his own hands to support his grandmother; when he had leisure he read books.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng lost his father early. The family was poor, and he plowed with his own hands to support his grandmother; when he had leisure he read books.

sentences.zh: 時人未之奇也。

translations.literal: Men of the time did not yet regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries had not yet seen anything remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 江表取人，多以世族。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, in selecting men, they mostly relied on great clans.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, appointments went chiefly to great clans.

sentences.zh: 憕旣羇旅，不被擢用。

translations.literal: Cheng, being a stranger in the land, was not promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: As an outsider living abroad, Cheng went unnoticed and unappointed.

sentences.zh: 然負才使氣，未嘗趣世祿之門。

translations.literal: Yet he relied on his talent and was proud by nature; he never went to the gates of those who dispensed worldly salary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relied on his talent and was proud by nature; he never went to the gates of men who dispensed worldly salary.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將京兆韋潛度謂憕曰：「君門地非下，身材不劣，何不憕裾數參吏部？

translations.literal: Left Palace Gentleman Wei Qiandu of Jingzhao said to Cheng: "Your family standing is not low, and your person is not inferior — why not lift your robe and visit the Ministry of Personnel several times?
translations.idiomatic: Left palace gentleman Wei Qiandu of Jingzhao said to Cheng, "Your family standing is not low, and your person is not inferior — why not lift your robe and visit the Ministry of Personnel several times?

sentences.zh: 」憕曰：「『世冑躡高位，英俊沉下僚』，古人以為歎息。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: " 'Clansmen tread high rank; the able sink to low posts' — the ancients sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng replied, " 'Clansmen tread high rank; the able sink to low posts' — the ancients sighed over this.

sentences.zh: 竊所未能也。

translations.literal: Privately, I cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: I myself cannot do it.

sentences.zh: 」潛度告人曰：「此年少極慷慨，但不遭時耳。」

translations.literal: " Qiandu told others: "This young man is extremely high-minded; he simply has not met the right time."
translations.idiomatic: " Qiandu told others, "This young man is extremely high-minded; he simply has not met the right time."

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，杖策還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he leaned on his staff and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he took up his staff and walked home to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，憕從祖真度與族祖安都擁徐、兗歸魏，其子懷儁見憕，甚相親善。

translations.literal: Before this, Cheng's collateral elder Zhendu and clan elder Andu had brought Xu and Yan over to Wei; Andu's son Huaijun met Cheng and was very close and friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Cheng's collateral elder Zhendu and clan elder Andu had brought Xu and Yan over to Wei; Andu's son Huaijun met Cheng and became very close to him.

sentences.zh: 屬爾朱榮廢立，遂還河東，止懷儁家。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong deposed and enthroned emperors, Cheng returned to Hedong and stayed at Huaijun's house.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong began deposing and installing emperors, Cheng retreated to Hedong and lodged with Huaijun.

sentences.zh: 不交人物，終日讀書，手自抄略，將二百卷。

translations.literal: He did not associate with others, read all day, and copied extracts with his own hand — nearly two hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He did not associate with others, read all day, and copied extracts in his own hand — nearly two hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 唯郡守元襲，時相要屈，與之抗禮。

translations.literal: Only the prefect Yuan Xi occasionally invited and detained him, and Cheng treated him as an equal.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prefect Yuan Xi would sometimes summon him and keep him awhile; Cheng received him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 懷儁每曰：「汝還鄉里，不營產業，不肯取妻，豈復欲南乎？

translations.literal: Huaijun often said: "You return to your home district, do not build up property, and refuse to take a wife — do you still mean to go south?
translations.idiomatic: Huaijun often said, "You return to your home district, build no property, and refuse to take a wife — do you still mean to go south?

sentences.zh: 」憕亦恬然自處，不改其舊。

translations.literal: " Cheng also lived at ease and did not change his old ways.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng remained untroubled in his ways and changed nothing of his former life.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，拜給事中，加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he was appointed attendant within the gates, with added rank General Who Subdues Waves.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai he was appointed attendant within the gates, with added rank general who subdues waves.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起兵，憕乃東游陳、梁間，謂族人孝通曰：「高歡阻兵陵上，喪亂方始。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi raised troops, Cheng traveled east among Chen and Liang and said to his clansman Xiaotong: "Gao Huan blocks the armies and lords it over his sovereign; disorder has only begun.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops, Cheng traveled east among Chen and Liang and said to his clansman Xiaotong, "Gao Huan blocks the armies and lords it over his sovereign; disorder has only begun.

sentences.zh: 關中形勝之地，必有霸王居之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is a land of strategic strength; there must be a hegemon who will dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is a land of strategic strength; a hegemon is sure to hold it.

sentences.zh: 」乃與孝通俱游長安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Xiaotong together traveled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " So he and his clansman Xiaotong went together to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅聞之，召為行臺郎中，除鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Hou Mo Chen Yue heard of it, summoned him as mobile headquarters gentleman, and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Mo Chen Yue heard of it, he summoned Cheng as mobile headquarters gentleman and made him general who pacifies the distance and commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 及悅害賀拔岳，軍人咸相慶慰。

translations.literal: When Yue killed Heba Yue, the soldiers all congratulated and comforted one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue murdered Heba Yue, the troops all congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 憕獨謂所親曰：「悅才略本寡，輒害良將，敗亡之事，其則不遠。

translations.literal: Cheng alone told his intimates: "Yue's talent and strategy were meager to begin with; he rashly killed a good general — his ruin is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng alone told those close to him, "Yue never had much talent or strategy; by rashly killing a fine general he has brought ruin near.

sentences.zh: 吾屬今卽為人所虜，何慶慰之有乎！

translations.literal: We are about to become others' captives — what is there to congratulate and be comforted about!
translations.idiomatic: We are about to become someone else's prisoners — what is there to celebrate!

sentences.zh: 」聞者以憕言為然，乃有憂色。

translations.literal: " Those who heard thought Cheng's words correct and showed anxious faces.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard him thought Cheng was right and looked worried.

sentences.zh: 尋而太祖平悅，引憕為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Progenitor pacified Yue and brought Cheng in as recording-secretary adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai crushed Yue and made Cheng recording secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，授征虜將軍、中散大夫，封夏陽縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was granted General Who Captures the Enemy, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and enfeoffed Baron of Xiayang county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Cheng was made general who captures the enemy and grand master of palace attendance, enfeoffed as baron of Xiayang with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝卽位，拜中書侍郎，加安東將軍，增邑百戶，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei took the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Vice Gentleman, given the added rank of General Who Pacifies the East, increased fief by a hundred households, and advanced to count.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Cheng was appointed secretariat vice gentleman, given the added rank of general who pacifies the east, increased by a hundred households, and raised to count.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，宣光、清徽殿初成，憕為之頌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, when the Xuanguang and Qinghui halls were first completed, Cheng composed eulogies for them.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 4, when the Xuanguang and Qinghui halls were first finished, Cheng wrote eulogies for them.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝又造二欹器。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei also had two tilting vessels made.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also had two tilting vessels made.

sentences.zh: 一為二仙人共持一缽，同處一盤，缽蓋有山，山有香氣，一仙人又持金瓶以臨器上，以水灌山，則出於瓶而注乎器，煙氣通發山中，謂之仙人欹器。

translations.literal: One was two immortals jointly holding a bowl, both on one dish; the bowl cover had a mountain with fragrance; one immortal also held a golden flask above the vessel; when water was poured on the mountain it flowed from the flask into the vessel, and smoke issued through the mountain — it was called the Immortals' Tilting Vessel.
translations.idiomatic: One showed two immortals holding a shared bowl on one dish; the bowl's lid bore a fragrant mountain, and one immortal held a golden flask above the vessel; when water was poured on the mountain it ran from the flask into the vessel and smoke rose through the mountain — this was called the Immortals' Tilting Vessel.

sentences.zh: 一為二荷同處一盤，相去盈尺，中有蓮下垂器上，以水注荷，則出於蓮而盈乎器，為鳧鴈蟾蜍以飾之，謂之水芝欹器。

translations.literal: One was two lotuses on one dish, a full chi apart; a lotus hung down over the vessel; when water was poured on the lotus it flowed from the lotus and filled the vessel; ducks, geese, and toads were used as ornament — it was called the Water Lotuses Tilting Vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The other showed two lotuses on one dish a full chi apart, with a lotus hanging down over the vessel; when water was poured on the lotus it flowed out and filled the vessel, ornamented with ducks, geese, and toads — this was called the Water Lotuses Tilting Vessel.

sentences.zh: 二盤各處一床，缽圓而床方，中有人，言三才之象也。

translations.literal: The two dishes each rested on a stand; the bowl was round and the stand square, with a human figure between them — representing Heaven, Earth, and Man.
translations.idiomatic: Each dish stood on its own stand; the bowl was round and the stand square, with a human figure between them to represent heaven, earth, and man.

sentences.zh: 皆置清徽殿前。

translations.literal: Both were placed before the Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Both were set before the Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 器形似觥而方，滿則平，溢則傾。

translations.literal: The vessels resembled a square gong; when full they levelled, when overflowing they tipped.
translations.idiomatic: The vessels were square like a gong: full they stood level, overflowing they tipped.

sentences.zh: 憕各為作頌。

translations.literal: Cheng composed eulogies for each.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wrote a eulogy for each.

sentences.zh: 大統初，儀制多闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong many rites and regulations were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong many rites and regulations were still missing.

sentences.zh: 太祖令憕與盧辯、檀翥等參定之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Cheng together with Lu Bian, Tan Zhu, and others to consult on and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Cheng, together with Lu Bian, Tan Zhu, and others, to draft and codify them.

sentences.zh: 自以流離世故，不聽音樂。

translations.literal: Because he had been displaced by worldly upheaval, he would not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Having been uprooted by the turmoil of the age, he would not listen to music.

sentences.zh: 雖幽室獨處，嘗有戚容。

translations.literal: Even alone in a quiet room he often wore a sorrowful face.
translations.idiomatic: Even alone in a quiet room he often looked sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 後坐事死。

translations.literal: Later he was executed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 子舒嗣，官至禮部下大夫、儀同大將軍、聘陳使副。

translations.literal: His son Shu succeeded; he reached the ranks of Lesser Grand Master in the Ministry of Rites, Equal-Protocol Grand General, and deputy envoy on the mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu succeeded him and rose to lesser grand master in the Ministry of Rites, equal-protocol grand general, and deputy envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 薛寘，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Zhi was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhi came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖遵彥，魏平遠將軍、河東郡守、安邑侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zunyan was Wei General Who Pacifies the Distance, Administrator of Hedong commandery, and Marquis of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zunyan had served Wei as general who pacifies the distance, administrator of Hedong commandery, and marquis of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 父乂，尚書吏部郎、清河廣平二郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel's Left Bureau and Administrator of Qinghe and Guangping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was a gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and administrator of Qinghe and Guangping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為侯，增邑五百戶，轉御正中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to marquis, increased fief by five hundred households, and transferred to Middle Grand Master in the Office of Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Zhi was raised to marquis, given five hundred additional households, and made middle grand master in the Office of Rectification.

sentences.zh: 時前中書監盧柔，學業優深，文藻華贍，而寘與之方駕，故世號曰盧、薛焉。

translations.literal: At the time former Secretariat Supervisor Lu Rou had deep and superior learning and splendid literary talent; Zhi matched him as an equal, so the age called them Lu and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the former secretariat supervisor Lu Rou was deeply learned and richly gifted in letters; Zhi stood equal with him, so the age spoke of Lu and Xue together.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，出為淅州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening-Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and sent out as Inspector of Xi Province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and posted as inspector of Xi Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post.

sentences.zh: 吏民哀惜之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈虞州刺史，諡曰理。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Yu Province; posthumous title Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yu Province with the posthumous title Li.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆二十餘卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His literary compositions, more than twenty scrolls, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty scrolls of his writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 又撰《西京記》三卷，引據該洽，世稱其博聞焉。

translations.literal: He also compiled Records of the Western Capital in three scrolls; its citations were thorough and comprehensive, and the age praised his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Records of the Western Capital in three scrolls; its citations were thorough, and the age praised his wide learning.

sentences.zh: 寘性至孝，雖年齒已衰，職務繁廣，至於溫凊之禮，朝夕無違。

translations.literal: Zhi was extremely filial by nature; though advanced in years and burdened with many duties, in the rites of warmth and coolness he never failed morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was deeply filial by nature; though old and burdened with heavy duties, he never missed morning or evening the rites of asking after his parents' warmth and coolness.

sentences.zh: 當時以此稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ming inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 大象末，儀同大將軍、清水郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he held the ranks of Equal-Protocol Grand General and Administrator of Qingshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he held the ranks of equal-protocol grand general and administrator of Qingshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 李昶，頓丘臨黃人也，小名那。

translations.literal: Li Chang was a native of Linhuang in Dunqiu; his childhood name was Na.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang came from Linhuang in Dunqiu; his childhood name was Na.

sentences.zh: 祖彪，名重魏朝，為御史中尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Biao had a weighty name in Wei and served as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Biao was a man of great standing in Wei and served as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 父游，亦有才行，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: His father You also had talent and conduct and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was also talented and upright and won praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 游兄志，為南荊州刺史，游隨從至州。

translations.literal: You's elder brother Zhi was Inspector of South Jing Province; You followed him to the province.
translations.idiomatic: You's elder brother Zhi was inspector of South Jing Province, and You followed him there.

sentences.zh: 屬爾朱之亂，與志俱奔江左。

translations.literal: During the Erzhu turmoil they fled together with Zhi to the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: During the Erzhu upheaval he fled south with Zhi to the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 昶性峻急，不雜交遊。

translations.literal: Chang was stern and quick-tempered by nature and did not mix in social visiting.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was stern and impatient by nature and kept to himself.

sentences.zh: 幼年已解屬文，有聲洛下。

translations.literal: Even in childhood he could compose literature and had a reputation in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he could write and was already known in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽創置明堂，昶年十數歲，為《明堂賦》。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang was newly building the Bright Hall; Chang, in his mid-teens, wrote a "Rhapsody on the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was building the Bright Hall, Chang, still in his mid-teens, wrote a Rhapsody on the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 雖優洽未足，而才制可觀。

translations.literal: Though not yet fully polished, his talent and composition were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: It was not yet fully polished, but his talent and craft were evident.

sentences.zh: 見者咸曰「有家風矣」。

translations.literal: All who saw it said, "He has his family's style."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who read it said, "He has his family's gift."

sentences.zh: 初謁太祖，太祖深奇之，厚加資給，令入太學。

translations.literal: On first audience with the Grand Progenitor he was greatly admired, generously subsidized, and ordered into the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: On his first audience with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai he was greatly admired, richly subsidized, and sent into the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 太祖每見學生，必問才行於昶。

translations.literal: Whenever the Grand Progenitor saw students he always asked Chang about their talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai met students he asked Chang about their talent and character.

sentences.zh: 昶神情清悟，應對明辨，太祖每稱歎之。

translations.literal: Chang's expression was clear and penetrating; his responses were sharp and discriminating; the Grand Progenitor always praised and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was quick and clear-minded in speech; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai always praised him.

sentences.zh: 綏德公陸通盛選僚寀，請以昶為司馬，太祖許之。

translations.literal: Duke of Suide Lu Tong chose staff with great care and asked that Chang serve as marshal; the Grand Progenitor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, Duke of Suide, chose his staff with great care and asked that Chang serve as marshal; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai agreed.

sentences.zh: 昶雖年少，通特加接待，公私之事，咸取決焉。

translations.literal: Though Chang was young, Tong especially welcomed him; public and private affairs alike were decided through him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chang was young, Tong treated him with special favor, and public and private affairs alike were decided through him.

sentences.zh: 又兼二千石郎中，典儀注。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as Gentleman of the Two-Thousand-Shi Bureau and managed ceremonial precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as gentleman of the two-thousand-shi bureau and keeper of ceremonial precedents.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官郎中、相州大中正、丞相府東合祭酒、中軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Court of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Xiang Province, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Chancellor's Headquarters, General of the Central Army, and Silver-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to gentleman of the Court of Justice, chief rectifier of Xiang Province, libationer of the chancellor's eastern pavilion, general of the central army, and silver-gleam grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 昶雖處郎官，太祖恆欲以書記委之。

translations.literal: Though Chang held a gentleman's post, the Grand Progenitor always wished to entrust written records to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chang held a gentleman's rank, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai always wanted to put written records in his hands.

sentences.zh: 於是以昶為丞相府記室參軍、著作郎，修國史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Chang recording-secretary adjutant on the chancellor's staff and Gentleman of Compositions, editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore made Chang recording secretary on the chancellor's staff and gentleman of compositions, editing the national history.

sentences.zh: 轉大行臺郎中、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Grand Mobile Headquarters and Secretariat Vice Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the grand mobile headquarters and secretariat vice gentleman.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉黃門侍郎，封臨黃縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed Count of Linhuang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant gentleman in the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed as count of Linhuang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂昶曰：「卿祖昔在中朝，為御史中尉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once said to Chang: "Your grandfather in the central dynasty was Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told Chang, "Your grandfather in the central court was censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 卿操尚貞固，理應不墜家風。

translations.literal: Your integrity and steadfast conduct should surely not fall from your family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Your integrity and firmness of character ought not to fall from your family's tradition.

sentences.zh: 但孤以中尉彈劾之官，愛憎所在，故未卽授卿耳。

translations.literal: But I, because the censor-in-chief's office of impeachment attracts likes and dislikes, have not yet conferred it on you.
translations.idiomatic: But because the censor-in-chief's office of impeachment invites likes and dislikes, I have not yet given it to you.

sentences.zh: 然此職久曠，無以易卿。

translations.literal: Yet this post has long been vacant, and there is no one to replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the post has long stood empty, and no one can take your place.

sentences.zh: 」乃奏昶為御史中尉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon memorialized to make Chang Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized to make Chang censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was given Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was given bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers, and the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜內史下大夫，進爵為侯，增邑五百戶，遷內史中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed Lower Grand Master in the Inner Scribe's Office, advanced to marquis, increased fief by five hundred households, and transferred to Middle Grand Master in the Inner Scribe's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he became lower grand master in the inner scribe's office, was raised to marquis with five hundred additional households, and moved to middle grand master in the inner scribe's office.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，行禦伯中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he acted as Middle Grand Master of the Office of Equine Pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shizong's reign he served as acting middle grand master of the Office of Equine Pasturage.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，除中外府司錄。

translations.literal: In Wucheng year 1 he was appointed Recorder of the Central and External Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 1 he was made recorder of the central and external offices.

sentences.zh: 保定初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding he was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opening-Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉御正中大夫。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was transferred to Middle Grand Master in the Office of Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was transferred to middle grand master in the Office of Rectification.

sentences.zh: 時以近侍清要，盛選國華，乃以昶及安昌西元則、中都公陸逞、臨淄公唐瑾等竝為納言。

translations.literal: At the time close attendants were pure and important posts; the finest talent of the realm was chosen, and Chang together with Yuan Ze of Anchang West, Lu Cheng Duke of Zhongdu, Tang Jin Duke of Linzi, and others were all made nayan.
translations.idiomatic: Because close attendance at court was a pure and important post, the finest men of the realm were chosen, and Chang together with Yuan Ze of Anchang West, Lu Cheng Duke of Zhongdu, Tang Jin Duke of Linzi, and others were all made nayan.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵為公，增邑通前一千三百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to duke, with total fief reaching one thousand three hundred households including prior grants.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to duke, with total fief including earlier grants reaching one thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為昌州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was sent out as Inspector of Chang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was posted as inspector of Chang Province.

sentences.zh: 在州遇疾，啟求入朝，詔許之。

translations.literal: Ill in the province, he memorialized asking to enter court; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill in the province, he memorialized asking to return to court, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 還未至京，卒於路。

translations.literal: Returning, before reaching the capital he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back, before he reached the capital, he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 時年五十。

translations.literal: He was fifty at the time.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈相瀛二州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Xiang and Ying provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Xiang and Ying provinces.

sentences.zh: 昶於太祖世已當樞要，兵馬處分，專以委之，詔冊文筆，皆昶所作也。

translations.literal: In the Grand Progenitor's time Chang already held a key post; disposition of armies and horses was entrusted to him alone, and all edicts, patent letters, and literary compositions were written by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, Chang already held a pivotal post; disposition of armies and horses was entrusted to him alone, and all edicts, enfeoffments, and state papers were his work.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執政，委任如舊。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power, his trust and appointment were as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu took power, his trust and appointment were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 昶常曰：「文章之事，不足流於後世，經邦致治，庶及古人。

translations.literal: Chang often said: "Literary matters are not enough to live on in later ages; governing the state and bringing order — that one may hope to match the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Chang often said, "Literary work is not enough to survive in later ages; governing the state and bringing order — that one may hope to match the ancients.

sentences.zh: 」故所作文筆，了無藳草。

translations.literal: " Therefore the compositions he wrote left no drafts whatever.
translations.idiomatic: " So the writings he produced left no drafts at all.

sentences.zh: 唯留心政事而已。

translations.literal: He attended only to government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his mind only to government affairs.

sentences.zh: 又以父在江南，身寓關右，自少及終，不飲酒聽樂。
