translations.literal: Because his father was in Jiangnan while he himself lived in Guanxi, from youth to death he neither drank wine nor listened to music.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father remained in Jiangnan while he lived in Guanxi, from youth to death he neither drank wine nor listened to music.

sentences.zh: 時論以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Public opinion praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子丹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dan inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 時有高平檀翥，字鳳翔。

translations.literal: At the time there was Tan Zhu of Gaoping, styled Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Tan Zhu of Gaoping, courtesy name Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，善屬文，能鼓瑟。

translations.literal: He loved reading, was skilled at literary composition, and could play the se zither.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading, wrote well, and could play the se zither.

sentences.zh: 早為琅邪王誦所知。

translations.literal: Early on he was known to Wang Song, Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he was noticed by Wang Song, Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 年十九，為魏孝明帝挽郎。

translations.literal: At nineteen he was a mourning attendant at Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he served as a mourning attendant at Emperor Xiaoming's funeral.

sentences.zh: 其後司州牧、城陽王元徽以翥為從事，非其好也。

translations.literal: Later the Regional Governor of Si Province, Prince Yuan Hui of Chengyang, made Zhu a staff officer — not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Yuan Hui of Chengyang, regional governor of Si Province, made Zhu a staff officer — work he did not care for.

sentences.zh: 尋謝病，客遊三輔。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded illness and traveled as a guest in the Three Metropolises region.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and traveled as a guest in the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 時毛

translations.literal: At the time Mao
translations.idiomatic: In those days Mao

translations.literal: (Dun) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Dun]

sentences.zh: 〔遐〕為行臺，鎮北雍州，表翥為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: [emended: Xia] was mobile headquarters, garrisoning northern Yong Province, and memorialized Zhu as mobile headquarters gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was mobile headquarters, garrisoning northern Yong Province, and memorialized to make Zhu mobile headquarters gentleman.

sentences.zh: 會爾朱天光東拒齊神武，翥隨赴洛。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang went east to oppose Gao Huan of Northern Qi, Zhu followed him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched east to oppose Gao Huan, Zhu followed him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 除西兗州錄事參軍，歷司空田曹參軍，加鎮遠將軍，兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Appointed recording adjutant of West Yan Province; served as field-bureau adjutant under the Minister of Works; given the added rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance; concurrently Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made recording adjutant of West Yan Province, then field-bureau adjutant under the Minister of Works, given the added rank of general who pacifies the distance, and concurrently palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 臺中表奏，皆翥為之。

translations.literal: All memorials and reports in the censorate were written by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Every memorial and report in the censorate was Zhu's work.

sentences.zh: 尋副毛鴻賓鎮潼關，加前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he served under Mao Hongbin garrisoning Tong Pass; given the added ranks of Vanguard General and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served under Mao Hongbin at Tong Pass and was given the added ranks of vanguard general and grand master of palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，賜爵高唐縣子，兼中書舍人，修國史，加鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west he was granted Viscount of Gaotang county, concurrently Secretariat Draft Writer, editing the national history, and given the added rank of General Who Stabilizes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west he was enfeoffed viscount of Gaotang, made secretariat draft writer and editor of the national history, and given the added rank of general who stabilizes the army.

sentences.zh: 後坐談論輕躁，為黃門侍郎徐招所駁，死於廷尉獄。

translations.literal: Later, because of careless and rash talk, he was impeached by Attendant Gentleman in the Yellow Gate Xu Zhao and died in the Court of Justice prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for careless and rash talk, he was impeached by attendant gentleman in the Yellow Gate Xu Zhao and died in the Court of Justice prison.

sentences.zh: 元偉字猷道，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Wei, styled Youdao, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei, courtesy name Youdao, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 魏昭成之後。

translations.literal: A descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忠，尚書左僕射，城陽王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong was left vice director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhong had been left vice director of the masters of writing and Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 祖盛，通直散騎常侍，城陽公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng was regular attendant of direct communication of the scattered riders and Duke of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng held the ranks of regular attendant of direct communication of the scattered riders and duke of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 父順，以左衛將軍從魏孝武西遷，拜中書監、雍州刺史、開府儀同三司，封濮陽王。

translations.literal: His father Shun, as general of the left guard following Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in moving west, was appointed overseer of the Secretariat, inspector of Yong Province, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shun, serving as general of the left guard when Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fled west, was made overseer of the secretariat, inspector of Yong Province, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 偉少好學，有文雅。

translations.literal: Wei in youth loved learning and had literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wei loved learning and had literary polish.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At coming of age he was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier of the scattered riders.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he was made supernumerary attendant cavalier of the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 以侍從之勞，賜爵高陽縣伯。

translations.literal: For toil in attendance on the sovereign, he was granted the title Baron of Gaoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service as an attendant he was granted the title baron of Gaoyang county.

sentences.zh: 大統初，拜伏波將軍、度支郎中，領太子舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was appointed general who subdues waves, gentleman of revenue, and concurrently led as secretariat aide in the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he was made general who subdues waves and gentleman of revenue, and also served as secretariat aide in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷太子庶子，領兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to vice tutor of the heir apparent and concurrently led as director in the ministry of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became vice tutor of the heir apparent and also served as director in the ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 尋拜東南道行臺右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed right aide of the southeast route mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made right aide of the southeast route mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry and equal in protocol to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以魏氏宗室，進爵南安郡王，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Because he was of the Yuan imperial clan, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Nan'an commandery with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the Yuan imperial clan, he was raised to prince of Nan'an commandery with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除幽州都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed chief administrator of the Yongzhou area headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made chief administrator of the Yongzhou area headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥伐蜀，以偉為司錄。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Wei was made chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong marched against Shu, Wei was appointed chief recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 書檄文記，皆偉之所為。

translations.literal: Letters, proclamations, documents, and records were all Wei's work.
translations.idiomatic: Every dispatch, proclamation, and record of the campaign was written by Wei.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，以功增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, his fief was increased by five hundred households for merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, his fief was increased by five hundred households for his service.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜師氏下大夫，爵隨例降，改封淮南縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed lower grand master in the Office of Masters; his noble rank was reduced according to regulation, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huainan county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made lower grand master in the Office of Masters; his title was reduced by regulation and changed to duke of Huainan county.

sentences.zh: 偉性溫柔，好虛靜。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was gentle and mild; he loved quiet and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was gentle by nature and loved quiet and repose.

sentences.zh: 居家不治生業。

translations.literal: At home he did not manage property for livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: At home he did not trouble himself with earning a living.

sentences.zh: 篤學愛文，政事之暇，未嘗棄書。

translations.literal: Deeply devoted to learning and fond of literature, in the intervals of public affairs he never put books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to learning and fond of literature, he never set books aside even in the midst of public business.

sentences.zh: 謹慎小心，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, he had no friction with things.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and cautious, he gave offense to no one.

sentences.zh: 時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 初自鄴還也，庾信贈其詩曰：「虢亡垂棘反，齊平寶鼎歸。

translations.literal: When first returning from Ye, Yu Xin presented him a poem saying: "When Guo perished, Chuiji returned; when Qi was pacified, the precious tripod came home.
translations.idiomatic: When he first returned from Ye, Yu Xin gave him a poem that read, "When Guo fell, Chuiji came back; when Qi was pacified, the precious tripod returned home.

sentences.zh: 」其為辭人所重如此。

translations.literal: " So highly was he valued by men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which men of letters held him.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖天縱寬仁，性罕猜忌。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor by nature was broad and generous and rarely suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was generous by nature and seldom suspicious.

sentences.zh: 元氏戚屬，竝保全之，內外任使，布於列職。

translations.literal: Yuan kinsmen were all preserved; within and without they were appointed and employed, spread through the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan kinsmen were all kept safe; inside and outside the court they were appointed to posts throughout the ranks.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐祚，無替前緒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he did not alter the earlier course.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he did not change this policy.

sentences.zh: 明、武纘業，亦遵先志。

translations.literal: Emperors Ming and Wu continued the enterprise and likewise followed the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Ming and Wu carried on the work and likewise followed their predecessor's intent.

sentences.zh: 雖天厭魏德，鼎命已遷，枝葉榮茂，足以逾於前代矣。

translations.literal: Although Heaven had tired of Wei's virtue and the mandate of the tripod had shifted, the branches and leaves flourished luxuriantly — enough to surpass the former age.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven had turned from Wei's virtue and the imperial mandate had passed elsewhere, the Yuan line flourished as never before.

sentences.zh: 然簡牘散亡，事多湮沒。

translations.literal: Yet documents were scattered and lost, and many affairs sank into oblivion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet records were scattered and lost, and many deeds sank into oblivion.

sentences.zh: 今錄其名位可知者，附於此云。

translations.literal: Now those whose names and offices are known are recorded and appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose names and offices are still known are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 柱國大將軍、太傅、大司徒、廣陵王元欣。

translations.literal: Pillar grand general, grand tutor, grand steward, Prince of Guangling Yuan Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar grand general, grand tutor, grand steward, Prince of Guangling — Yuan Xin.

sentences.zh: 柱國大將軍、特進、尚書令、少師、義陽王元子孝。

translations.literal: Pillar grand general, specially advanced, director of the masters of writing, junior preceptor, Prince of Yiyang Yuan Zixiao.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar grand general, specially advanced, director of the masters of writing, junior preceptor, Prince of Yiyang — Yuan Zixiao.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、馮翊王元季海。

translations.literal: Vice director of the masters of writing, Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the masters of writing, Prince of Fengyi — Yuan Jihai.

sentences.zh: 七兵尚書、陳郡王元玄，

translations.literal: Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery Yuan Xuan,
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery — Yuan Xuan,

sentences.zh: 大將軍、淮安王元育，

translations.literal: Grand general, Prince of Huai'an Yuan Yu,
translations.idiomatic: Grand general, Prince of Huai'an — Yuan Yu,

sentences.zh: 大將軍、梁王元儉，

translations.literal: Grand general, Prince of Liang Yuan Jian,
translations.idiomatic: Grand general, Prince of Liang — Yuan Jian,

sentences.zh: 大將軍、尚書令、少保、小司徒、廣平郡公元贊，

translations.literal: Grand general, director of the masters of writing, junior guardian, lesser grand steward, Duke of Guangping commandery Yuan Zan,
translations.idiomatic: Grand general, director of the masters of writing, junior guardian, lesser grand steward, Duke of Guangping commandery — Yuan Zan,

sentences.zh: 大將軍、納言、小司空、荊州總管、安昌郡公元則，

translations.literal: Grand general, court censor, junior minister of works, area commander of Jing Province, Duke of Anchang commandery Yuan Ze,
translations.idiomatic: Grand general, court censor, junior minister of works, area commander of Jing Province, Duke of Anchang commandery — Yuan Ze,

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、少師、韓國公元羅，

translations.literal: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, junior preceptor, Duke of Han state Yuan Luo,
translations.idiomatic: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, junior preceptor, Duke of Han — Yuan Luo,

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、吏部尚書、魯郡公元正，

translations.literal: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, director of the ministry of personnel, Duke of Lu commandery Yuan Zheng,
translations.idiomatic: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, director of the ministry of personnel, Duke of Lu commandery — Yuan Zheng,

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、中書監、洵州刺史、宜都郡公元顏子，

translations.literal: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, overseer of the secretariat, inspector of Xun Province, Duke of Yidu commandery Yuan Yanzi,
translations.idiomatic: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, overseer of the secretariat, inspector of Xun Province, Duke of Yidu commandery — Yuan Yanzi,

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、鄯州刺史、安樂縣公元壽，

translations.literal: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Shan Province, Duke of Anle county Yuan Shou,
translations.idiomatic: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, inspector of Shan Province, Duke of Anle county — Yuan Shou,

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、武衛將軍、遂州刺史、房陵縣公元審。

translations.literal: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, general of the martial guard, inspector of Sui Province, Duke of Fangling county Yuan Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant within, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal in protocol to the three excellencies, general of the martial guard, inspector of Sui Province, Duke of Fangling county — Yuan Shen.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖除暴寧亂，創業開基，昃食求賢，共康庶政。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Grand Progenitor removed violence and settled disorder, founded the enterprise and opened the foundation, ate at sunset and sought the worthy, together bringing peace to common governance.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai quelled violence and restored order, laid the foundations of the state, worked late into the evening seeking worthy men, and together with them brought the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 旣焚林而訪阮，亦牓道以求孫，可謂野無遺才，朝多君子。

translations.literal: Having burned the forest to visit Ruan, he also posted notices on the road to seek Sun — one may say in the wilds none of talent was left behind, and in the court many gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the forest to find Ruan and posted notices on the roads to seek Sun — so thoroughly did he hunt talent that none was overlooked in the land and the court was full of fine men.

sentences.zh: 蘇亮等並學稱該博，文擅雕龍，或揮翰鳳池，或著書麟閣，咸居祿位，各逞琳琅。

translations.literal: Su Liang and the rest alike were called thoroughly learned in scholarship, excelled in literary craft like "carving dragons"; some wielded the brush at the Phoenix Pool, some wrote books at the Unicorn Pavilion — all held salary offices, each displaying brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Su Liang and his fellows were all praised as broadly learned, masters of literary craft; some wrote at the Phoenix Pool, others compiled works at the Unicorn Pavilion — all held office and each shone with talent.

sentences.zh: 擬彼陳、徐，慚後生之可畏；

translations.literal: Compared with those Chen and Xu, one would feel shame at how formidable the younger generation is;
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the famous Chen and Xu, one would feel humbled by how formidable this younger generation was;

sentences.zh: 論其任遇，實當時之良選也。

translations.literal: speaking of their appointments and treatment, they were truly the fine choices of the age.
translations.idiomatic: and in their appointments and honors they were truly the best men of their time.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝有言：「古今文人，類不護細行。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once said: "Literary men ancient and modern, as a rule do not keep to petty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once said, "Writers ancient and modern, as a rule, do not trouble themselves with petty conduct.

sentences.zh: 」其呂思禮、薛憕之謂也？

translations.literal: " Does this refer to Lu Sili and Xue Cheng?
translations.idiomatic: " Was he not speaking of Lu Sili and Xue Cheng?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
